physicalDetails.detail: Old; weathered face; nose 'broken once and set crooked'. Wears a hat (takes it off at the sight of Millhaven, turns it in his hands, puts it back on). Sits the box of a flat farm wagon with plank sides, a sack across his knees against the cold. Brown cob in the shafts, feathered legs caked in mud to the knee, collar patched with sacking and twine. The wagon is empty but for a coil of rope and a folded sack; old grain dust packed grey into the cracks between the planks.

voiceMarkers.detail: Plain, short sentences in the common tongue; local, tired, courteous. 'Morning.', 'Where's everybody?', 'Dead. Millhaven? I was through here on market day. They were well enough then.', 'The ford. Down the valley.', 'All of them, far as I know... Barley's up a copper the measure, and they're crying about it, but they're buying. I'd not have thought it. Not Millhaven.', 'I come up for the mill every fortnight. Nothing for me here, then.', 'You'll not have passed a young fellow on the road? Coming down from your way, with a grain cart. New man. I've a mind to see what he looks like.', 'That's the truth.', 'May the stars keep your road.'

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Continue north up the empty street (he drives his wagon through the crossing and up the street beyond).
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Unstated on page. Plan intent (not shown): he is checking his work and his agent; Mal'Ganis plant per project notes.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Genial and unflustered after an initial shock; laughs 'short, through his nose' at Lyriel's remark.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Hauled back on the reins at the sight of bows; said 'Morning' to the bows; looked past them; took off his hat; asked 'Where's everybody?'.

Described the settlements south as trading and well; asked about the young grain-man; accepted Lyriel's answer; took in the line of horses once, front to back, 'the mage's borrowed mare sitting between them in the gap'; drove on north through the crossing.

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Sylvanas
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: No address; speaks to him as 'you' ('Don't water your horse here')

howHeAddressesOthers.pattern: 'Morning' (to the bows); 'You'll not have passed...' ; no names or titles.

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Hauls back on the reins; mouth goes slack first and then the rest of him catches up; takes his hat off; turns it in his hands; turns toward the inn door again as if to check; his eyes go once along the line of horses from front to back; slaps the reins on the cob's back to move on; does not look back (not stated).

knowledge.detail: Says he was 'through here on market day' (Millhaven) and they were 'well enough then'; says he comes up for the mill every fortnight; says the market at the ford was busy yesterday, smoke in every chimney the whole way up from the ford, barley up a copper. He asks after a young fellow with a grain cart, a new man, whom he has not met.

Told by Sylvanas that Millhaven is dead for five days and not to touch the well. Told by Lyriel that the party passed nobody, that the girl spoke of a newer grain seller, and that they will watch for him going south.

arc.currentPosition: Rolls off north into the empty Millhaven street after saying 'May the stars keep your road'. PLAN-ONLY (not on page): project notes identify him as the Mal'Ganis plant (investigation-arc.md) and say his eyes on the line of horses and the spacing relate to the Ch9 ward; the prose does not say or hint this. The prose frames him as an ordinary, forgettable, useful local source.
